Box-Cox Transformation

Source: R/stats.R
boxcox_transform.Rd

Applies a Box-Cox transformation to analytical results within groups.

Usage

boxcox_transform(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
boxcox_transform(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  objective_name = "PPCC",
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
boxcox_transform(
  df,
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  objective_name = "PPCC",
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

objective_name

Character string specifying the optimization criterion passed to [EnvStats::boxcox()].

keep_data_object

Logical indicating whether the complete Box-Cox result object should be retained.

Value

The original data with additional columns:

.boxcox_transform

Box-Cox transformed analytical result.

.boxcox_lambda

Estimated Box-Cox transformation parameter.

boxcox

Full Box-Cox optimization result object when `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

Details

Transformation parameters are estimated independently for each group using [EnvStats::boxcox()]. Transformed values are calculated using [EnvStats::boxcoxTransform()].

Existing analytical results are preserved. Transformed values are returned in a new `.boxcox_transform` column together with the estimated transformation parameter `.boxcox_lambda`.

If the input is grouped using [dplyr::group_by()], transformations are performed within the existing groups.

For ungrouped `env_schema` objects, transformations are performed by:

  • location

  • analyte

  • analysis unit

For ungrouped `data.frame` inputs, data are first converted to an env_schema object and transformations are performed separately by location, analyte, and analysis unit.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, Box-Cox transformations are performed using standardized analytical results stored in `.analysis_result`.

Existing `dplyr::group_by()` groups are preserved.

When the input is not grouped, transformations are performed by:

  • location

  • analyte

  • analysis unit

Schema metadata are preserved.

Examples

gw |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    location_id,
    param_name
  ) |>
  boxcox_transform()
